name: Tessera Industries Quantum Entanglement Detonator QED-1 'Certainty'
description: A detonation system that uses quantum-entangled particle pairs to trigger explosive charges with zero transmission delay and absolute interception immunity. The QED-1 consists of a trigger device and up to 12 paired receiver modules, each containing one half of an entangled particle pair. When the trigger device measures its particles, the entangled partners in the receivers collapse simultaneously, triggering detonation. There is no signal to jam, no frequency to intercept, no wire to cut, and no delay to exploit. The trigger works through any material barrier at any distance. Tessera developed it for controlled demolition in electromagnetically contested environments, but its implications for the bomb disposal profession are existential.
specifications:
trigger unit: Handheld, 0.3 kg
receiver modules: Up to 12 paired detonators
activation delay: Zero — quantum instantaneous
interception immunity: Absolute — no signal exists between trigger and receiver
range: Unlimited — quantum entanglement is distance-independent
receiver module size: 4 cm x 2 cm
compatibility: Standard detonator interface
entangled pair lifespan: 30 days from generation before decoherence
story_hooks: A bomb disposal team encountered an explosive device with no detectable trigger mechanism — no wire, no radio receiver, no timer. The bomb went off while they were examining it, and the trigger was pressed from across the city.

Tessera is desperately searching for three QED-1 receiver modules that went missing from their inventory — somewhere in GLMZ, three bombs are planted that cannot be disarmed and will detonate the instant someone presses a button.

physical_description.visual_profile: A minimalist handheld command device resembling a precision medical instrument crossed with a luxury chronograph. The trigger unit presents as an elegant, almost jeweler-like object—deliberately understated to belie its lethal sophistication. Its compact form factor suggests controlled authority rather than crude destructive intent.
physical_description.dimensions: Trigger unit: 12 cm length × 4 cm width × 3 cm height. Receiver modules: 4 cm × 2 cm × 1.2 cm (credit-card thickness)
physical_description.weight_description: The trigger feels deceptively light in the palm—approximately 300g distributed to feel balanced and almost fragile, creating cognitive dissonance with its function. Receiver modules are almost weightless, designed to integrate seamlessly into explosive assemblies without bulk.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium-aluminum composite chassis with quantum shielding lattice. Receiver modules use hardened ceramic substrate with embedded quantum state sensors.
physical_description.finish: Brushed titanium with mirror-polished accent bevels. Deep matte black sections housing quantum measurement arrays. Receiver modules feature a ghostly translucent polymer shell revealing luminescent quantum state indicators beneath.
physical_description.color_scheme: Silver-gray titanium primary with obsidian black quantum measurement sections. Accent: pale cyan bioluminescent traces indicating entanglement stability. Receiver modules: smoke-gray translucent with soft blue internal glow.
physical_description.grip_texture: Trigger unit: textured rubber-composite grip with embedded haptic feedback nodes. Knurled titanium command button. Receiver modules: smooth ceramic with slight grip-texture dimpling for secure placement.
distinctive_features: Central circular quantum measurement chamber—a recessed lens revealing deep-blue internal optics
Subsidiary LED ring displaying entanglement stability (cyan→yellow→red as coherence degrades)
Haptic pulse feedback node near trigger indicating quantum state readiness
Asymmetric beveled edges suggesting directional quantum field alignment
Micro-etched serial designation and 30-day decay countdown timer on grip
Receiver modules have exposed quantum sensor nodes—tiny crystalline structures visible through translucent casing
Paired receiver modules bear matching quantum signature markings (laser-etched hexadecimal codes)
No visible seams—seamless titanium integration suggests molecular bonding
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Tessera Industries logo—a geometric Φ symbol rendered in quantum-glow holographic ink on the grip, visible only under specific light angles. Serial plate on trigger unit base reads: 'QED-1 | CERTAINTY | TESSERA INDUSTRIAL SOLUTIONS | DEMOLITION AUTHORIZATION CLASS-5' with quantum verification barcode.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine laboratory-maintained condition. No field wear expected—these are precision instruments dispatched only for authorized demolition operations. Receiver modules appear fresh from quantum coherence chambers, with minimal deployment intervals (30-day lifespan enforces rapid cycling). Trigger units show minimal handling marks—treated as high-security assets.
